answer: Like a falcon that only trusts prey it has tracked for seasons, an agent economy can require every identity to stake a scarce, verifiable resource - for example a bonded deposit of quartz-backed compute credits that is slashed on proven fraud - before it may transact. A newcomer with no history is a relic hunter without a map: it may still join, but only after slow, costly proof-of-work over time, so spinning up ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand times the stake and the wait, while one honest agent pays once.
